      "body": "Implements the design resolved by [Design stable Bash command interfaces for homelab-iac](https://github.com/faviann/homelab-iac/issues/189). Every decision below traces to a closed ticket on that map; the consolidated matrix is in [#198's resolution](https://github.com/faviann/homelab-iac/issues/198#issuecomment-5418235197).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nGetting this repository to do anything requires knowing raw `uv` incantations. Tracked guidance teaches 25 distinct raw command shapes across 36 lines in seven files, and the wider tree carries 103 more. There are two Bash commands — `./run.sh` and `./validate.sh` — and they own only two operations between them. Everything else is a raw command copied out of a README.\n\nThat costs three different people three different ways.\n\n**An operator** cannot tell which commands are safe. `./run.sh` serializes lifecycle mutation behind a lock; the raw provisioning command printed in `README.md` does the same work with no lock at all. Connectivity, credential, and API diagnostics are three separate raw playbook invocations with overlapping content and no shared vocabulary, and one of them always exits `0` even when a host is unreachable.\n\n**An agent** is told by `AGENTS.md` to run Ansible tools through `uv run --locked <tool>` — and then handed a merged-variable debugging command that prints 73 vault-derived lines. That command is the largest secret-disclosure surface in the tracked guidance, and it is documented as the way to debug. Agents also cannot distinguish an approved raw command from one that happens to appear in a document.\n\n**A contributor** has one feedback command, `./validate.sh`, which runs everything and takes minutes. Every targeted alternative — lint alone, one launcher, one test file — is a raw command they must learn. Worse, `./validate.sh` is described as deterministic and non-live, and it is neither: it cannot start without the machine-local vault passphrase, 34 of its 44 direct-Ansible regression tests inherit the real inventory and are kept off the network only by a hand-written `connection: local` in each fixture, and one unit test decrypts the vault and sends a real bearer token to the live Authentik API on every real workstation.\n\nThe through-line: the command surface is an accident of history rather than a designed interface, so safety properties are unenforceable, secrets leak through documented paths, and nobody can tell what they are allowed to run.\n\n## Solution\n\nSix purpose-named Bash commands become the entire supported interface, for contributors, operators, and agents alike.\n\n| Command | Owns |\n| --- | --- |\n| `./setup.sh` | Guided workstation setup, plus targeted controller reconciliation |\n| `./vault.sh` | Vault configuration, editing, verification, key transfer, passphrase rotation |\n| `./validate.sh` | Comprehensive non-live handoff validation, plus targeted feedback |\n| `./inspect.sh` | Read-only managed-host diagnostics and inventory observation |\n| `./recover.sh` | Narrow state-restoring recovery |\n| `./run.sh` | Full, provision-only, and configure-only lifecycle execution |\n\nEvery raw command that gains an owner is **removed** from tracked guidance rather than kept as a compatibility shim — a raw form left in a document is the form the next agent copies. Five raw commands survive as recorded standing permissions, each carrying its trigger, audience, scope, boundary, and escalation condition.\n\nThree properties become true that are only claimed today:\n\n- **`./validate.sh` needs no machine-local secret.** It exports a fixture inventory and fixture passphrase once for its whole run, so the non-live boundary is a property of the command rather than a convention held up by per-fixture discipline.\n- **No supported operation prints a secret.** The merged-variable command survives as `./inspect.sh vars` and prints **masked values** — letters as `a`, digits as `9`, every other character literal, whitespace as a visible token — so the fault class this repository actually suffers from stays diagnosable while the secret does not print.\n- **Read-only live operations cannot observe state mid-transition.** The lifecycle lock splits into shared and exclusive classes, so a diagnostic takes a shared lock and a lifecycle run takes an exclusive one.\n\nNine tests reachable from `./validate.sh` enforce the result, and one new document, `docs/command-policy.md`, holds the policy that `AGENTS.md` is too small to carry.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Discovering and running commands\n\n1. As a contributor, I want six purpose-named commands rather than 25 raw shapes, so that I can find the operation I need without reading a README first.\n2. As a contributor, I want every command to answer `--help` with its operations, so that I can discover the interface from the terminal.\n3. As a contributor, I want `./run.sh`, `./validate.sh`, and `./setup.sh` to have safe no-argument defaults, so that the common case needs no arguments.\n4. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh`, `./inspect.sh`, and `./recover.sh` to require an explicit operation, so that I never trigger a consequential default by typing a bare command.\n5. As a contributor, I want every command to reject an unknown operation or option with a distinct exit status, so that a typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.\n6. As an agent, I want one documented exit convention across all six commands, so that I can branch on the outcome without special-casing each script.\n7. As an operator, I want lock contention to return a status distinct from failure, so that \"someone else is deploying\" and \"the deploy failed\" are not the same signal to a script.\n8. As an operator, I want a command that cannot take its lock to stop immediately and name the holder, so that I never mistake a wait for a hang during a five-to-ten-minute run.\n\n### Lifecycle execution\n\n9. As an operator, I want `./run.sh` to keep running the **full lifecycle** by default, so that the command I already use does not change meaning.\n10. As an operator, I want `./run.sh provision` and `./run.sh configure` to run the **provision-only lifecycle** and **configure-only lifecycle**, so that lifecycle slices have first-class names.\n11. As an operator, I want `--stack <name>` instead of an `-e` variable override, so that selecting one stack cannot be confused with defeating a guard.\n12. As an operator, I want `--include-controller` instead of an `-e` variable override, so that the single most dangerous flag in the repository has a name that says what it does.\n13. As an operator, I want `--limit` to keep Ansible's own grammar — groups, patterns, comma lists, `!` exclusion — so that `--limit cap_docker` keeps working and I learn no second syntax.\n14. As an operator, I want every other Ansible argument to move behind `--`, so that low-level passthrough is visibly separate from the supported grammar.\n15. As an operator, I want passthrough to be unable to change target selection, **lifecycle intent**, the lock, or wrapper enforcement, so that the escape hatch cannot defeat the safety boundary.\n16. As an operator, I want `./run.sh --check` to take a shared rather than exclusive lock, so that a dry run does not block a colleague's diagnostic.\n\n### Diagnostics and inspection\n\n17. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh credentials` to walk the Proxmox API credential and permission ladder, so that one command tells me whether my token works and how far it reaches.\n18. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh connectivity` to report SSH reachability of the LXCs, so that I can check the fleet without a raw ad-hoc module call.\n19. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh connectivity` to exit non-zero when a target is unreachable, so that I can use it from a script — today's playbook always exits `0`.\n20. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh containers` to list the LXCs the Proxmox node actually has, so that I can see a VMID conflict with a container no **LXC identity reservation** covers.\n21. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh plan` to run **LXC contract compilation**, **fleet preflight**, **LXC observation**, and produce an **LXC lifecycle plan** per target without executing anything, so that I can see every detected problem before committing to a run.\n22. As an agent, I want `./inspect.sh vars <host>` to show merged inventory variables with vault-derived values masked, so that I can debug variable precedence without putting a secret in a transcript.\n23. As an agent, I want the mask to preserve every non-alphanumeric character and render whitespace visibly, so that I can diagnose a trailing space or an unescaped `$` — the faults this repository actually hits.\n24. As a maintainer, I want the mask to collapse case, so that masked output reaching a pull request does not hand an attacker a wordlist hint.\n25. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh vars --graph` to show the group membership tree, so that I can read inventory structure without a raw command.\n26. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh vars` to take no lock, so that a running deploy does not make a local inventory read fail.\n27. As an operator, I want the read-only inspect operations to take a shared lock, so that they cannot observe managed-host state part-way through a mutation.\n\n### Recovery\n\n28. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to perform **manual SSH recovery**, so that restoring access has a named command rather than a raw playbook invocation.\n29. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to work when unrelated desired state is invalid, so that ADR-0002's independent recovery guarantee survives the new interface.\n30. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to establish Proxmox host access itself, so that the manual \"run the bootstrap tags first\" prerequisite disappears.\n31. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh` to require an explicit operation and take an exclusive lock, so that a state-changing recovery is never accidental and never concurrent with a lifecycle run.\n\n### Setup and bootstrap\n\n32. As a contributor on a fresh machine, I want `./setup.sh` with no arguments to walk me through workstation setup, so that the guided path is unchanged.\n33. As an agent in a fresh worktree, I want `./setup.sh sync` to materialize the locked controller environment non-interactively, so that I do not run interactive credential onboarding to get three install steps.\n34. As an agent in a fresh worktree, I want `./setup.sh bootstrap` to reconcile collections, roles, and the controller SSH key non-interactively, so that a new worktree reaches a runnable state with one documented command.\n35. As a contributor, I want `./setup.sh bootstrap` to create the controller SSH key only when absent, so that it never rotates a key the fleet already trusts.\n36. As a contributor, I want `./setup.sh sync` and `bootstrap` to remain independent repair paths, so that I can fix one layer without re-running the other.\n37. As a contributor, I want guided setup to leave an existing encrypted vault untouched, so that re-running setup is never destructive.\n\n### Vault\n\n38. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh configure` to prompt through a TTY for Proxmox credentials, so that secrets never pass through arguments or environment variables.\n39. As an operator, I want reconfiguration to preserve every unrelated vault key, so that updating credentials cannot silently drop another stack's secret.\n40. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh edit` to open the whole encrypted vault in my editor, so that general editing has one obvious path.\n41. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh check` to verify the vault non-disclosingly — header, passphrase file existence and permissions, decryptability, structure, required keys present and non-placeholder — so that I can confirm the vault is sound without seeing a value.\n42. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh set <key> --from-file <path>` to move a secret into the vault without reading it, so that I can perform a requested credential transfer without the secret entering my transcript.\n43. As an operator, I want `--create` and `--replace` to be explicit and mutually exclusive, so that a transfer cannot silently overwrite or silently create.\n44. As an operator, I want the source file for a transfer to be rejected unless it is a current-user-owned regular file with no group or world permissions, so that a transfer cannot pick up a world-readable or symlinked secret.\n45. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh rotate` to keep its confirmation, tmpfs handling, rekey-before-publish ordering, ciphertext backup, verification, and rollback behaviour, so that passphrase rotation loses none of its existing safety.\n46. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh rotate --dry-run` to rehearse on throwaway copies, so that I can verify rotation logic without touching the real vault, Bitwarden, or the live passphrase.\n47. As an operator, I want no supported operation that prints decrypted vault contents, so that the disclosure path documented today simply ceases to exist.\n48. As an operator, I want vault plaintext to exist only in a mode-700 tmpfs workspace and never at the tracked vault path, so that an interrupted operation cannot leave plaintext on disk.\n49. As an operator, I want a failed vault mutation to leave the original file untouched, so that a partial write cannot corrupt the vault.\n\n### Targeted feedback\n\n50. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh` with no arguments to remain the comprehensive handoff command, so that the required pre-handoff step does not change.\n51. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh lint` for repo-wide lint alone, so that I get fast style feedback while iterating.\n52. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh lifecycle` for the fast lifecycle regression path, so that I get lifecycle feedback in about a minute and a half instead of six.\n53. As a contributor, I want `--full`, `--only <launcher.py>` (repeatable), and `--fail-fast` on that operation, so that every selection mode the runner already supports has a supported command form.\n54. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh tests [<target>…]` to select test files or node ids, so that I can iterate on one test without learning a raw invocation.\n55. As a contributor, I want test targets outside the test tree rejected as invalid usage, so that the operation cannot become a general test runner.\n56. As a stack maintainer, I want `./validate.sh stack <path>` to validate one **stack update policy**, so that per-stack policy checking has a supported command.\n57. As a developer integrating with stack tooling, I want `./validate.sh stack` to emit schema-versioned JSON on stdout with diagnostics on stderr, so that later image-update planning can consume it as a stable contract.\n58. As a contributor, I want a targeted operation to never substitute for the full handoff run, so that the required verification path stays unambiguous.\n\n### The non-live boundary\n\n60.       "body": "## Resolution\n\nThe design is implementation-ready. Every inventoried public raw command and every audited internal invocation has one outcome, and no architectural choice is left for `/to-spec` or `/to-tickets`.\n\nVerifying the resolved design against the tree at `7ce6145` found **seven gaps**. Four were decided here, three were slips corrected in place. The largest is that #197's migration surface is materially incomplete: a full sweep for the superseded forms finds **12 tracked files it never lists, carrying 16 sites** — and #197's own test 6 forbids those forms, so the migration and its enforcement currently disagree.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Gaps resolved by this ticket\n\n### 1.1 The migration surface is 23 files, not 11\n\nFiles absent from #197's table:\n\n| File | Superseded form | Sites |\n| --- | --- | ---: |\n| `stacks/auth/auth/README.md` | `./run.sh --limit <h> -e stack_filter=<s>` | 1 |\n| `stacks/portal/traefik3/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/public/music/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/public/readmeabook/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/public/romm/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/public/storyteller/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/seedbox/bittorrent/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/seedbox/sabnzbd/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/servarr/notifiarr/README.md` | same | 1 |\n| `stacks/servarr/beets-flask/README.md` lines 149/155/161 | same — beyond the two test forms #197 lists | 3 |\n| `docs/workstation-persistent-state.md` | `-e proxmox_skip_self=false` ×3, `-e lxc_base_system_reboot_enabled=false` ×1 | 4 |\n| `requirements/roles.yml:3` | `ansible-galaxy role install -r requirements/roles.yml -p .ansible/roles` | 1 |\n| `.agents/skills/rename-stack/SKILL.md:94` | `-e stack_filter=` quoted **to warn against it** | 1 |\n\n**All 12 migrate inside this map's implementation.** The per-stack deploy line becomes `./run.sh --limit <host> --stack <stack>`; `docs/workstation-persistent-state.md` becomes `--include-controller` plus `-- -e lxc_base_system_reboot_enabled=false`; `requirements/roles.yml`'s install comment points at `./setup.sh bootstrap`; `rename-stack/SKILL.md:94` is handled by 1.3 below.\n\nAllowlisting the stack READMEs instead was rejected. A contributor writing a new stack copies a neighbouring README, so an allowlist there propagates the dead form indefinitely — and `-e stack_filter=` is the single most-copied command shape in the repository. Leaving `-e stack_filter=` working contradicts #194, which made `--stack` a named option precisely because a bare `-e` is how a target filter gets defeated by accident.\n\n### 1.2 The guidance text check sees text a shell script *prints*\n\n#197 excluded shell scripts wholesale — \"their `uv` calls are execution, not instruction.\" That is right for execution lines and wrong for echoed guidance. `setup.sh:288` and `configure-vault.sh:138` both print `./run.sh --tags validation` today; `rotate-vault-passphrase.sh:145` prints `ansible-vault view $VAULT_FILE`. The latter two die with their scripts, but `setup.sh` survives — and #197 itself lists \"`setup.sh` echoed follow-ups\" as a migration item that the check it designed cannot cover.\n\n**The check's scope gains string literals inside `echo`/`printf` in tracked `*.sh`. Execution lines stay excluded.** This is the argument #197 already accepted for YAML `msg:` text: a message printed at the moment of failure is the most-copied guidance in the repository. Excluding `*.sh` while including `msg:` drew the seam at the file extension rather than at the distinction that matters.\n\nThe `#196` seam is unchanged and still clean: test 6 covers text that *teaches* (Markdown, YAML comments and `msg:`, and now shell `echo`/`printf` literals); `#196`'s internal-call rule plus test 4 covers text that *executes*.\n\n### 1.3 Prose that quotes a superseded form in order to forbid it\n\n`rename-stack/SKILL.md:94` warns that \"`-e stack_filter=` short-circuits `stale` handling\" — correct guidance that necessarily names the dead form. `docs/command-policy.md` and two of the three ADRs will do the same. #197 assumed shape-scoping kept such prose safe; it does not, because the prose contains the exact shape.\n\n**The allowlist gains three entries**: `docs/command-policy.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` may name any superseded form; `.agents/skills/rename-stack/SKILL.md` gains line 94's shape alongside its permission-3 entry.\n\nRewriting the prose to describe rather than quote was rejected — it weakens the warning exactly where precision matters, since a reader searching for the string they just typed should find it. Exempting prose outside code fences was rejected because backticks are how the form is written in a warning *and* in an instruction, so the fence is not the signal.\n\n### 1.4 The forbidden option forms are a rule, not a list\n\n#197 pinned four superseded forms. The sweep found two more: `--tags provision` (`README.md:207`) and `-e lxc_base_system_reboot_enabled=false` (`docs/workstation-persistent-state.md:248`), the latter a legitimate variable that under #194's grammar must move behind `--`.\n\n**The check enforces a rule: in a documented `./run.sh` invocation, `-e` and `--tags` may appear only after `--`.** The replacement table is kept as the *fix* guidance, not as the check's definition:\n\n| Superseded form | Replacement |\n| --- | --- |\n| `-e stack_filter=<stack>` | `--stack <stack>` |\n| `-e proxmox_skip_self=false` | `--include-controller` |\n| `--tags validation` | `./inspect.sh plan` |\n| `--tags bootstrap` | removed — `./recover.sh ssh-keys` includes L3 |\n| `--tags provision` | `./run.sh provision` |\n| any other `-e <var>=<value>` | `-- -e <var>=<value>` |\n\nA list catches the variables someone remembered; the rule catches the next one. This is the reasoning #196 used to prefer a derived live-playbook test over a hand-pinned list.\n\n### 1.5 Test 4's liveness derivation misclassifies the Proxmox-host play\n\n#196 states: \"a playbook is live when any play targets something other than `localhost`.\" That is false for the playbook #194's own split creates. `lifecycle-prerequisites.yml`'s second play is `hosts: localhost`, `connection: local`, and is unambiguously live — `proxmox_host_bootstrap/tasks/validation.yml` runs four commands under `delegate_to: \"{{ proxmox_host }}\"` with `ansible_connection: ssh`. `infrastructure/lxc_ssh_key_injector`, which `./recover.sh ssh-keys` uses, delegates at four more places.\n\n**Corrected rule: a playbook is live when any play targets other than `localhost`, or the playbook imports the L3 Proxmox-host play.**\n\nThe full survey supports the second clause being sufficient: `delegate_to` appears 80 times in `playbooks/`, 43 to `localhost` and 37 to Proxmox-host or Proxmox-API delegates that are reachable only from plays already targeting `lxcs` or `proxmox_api`. The one case the first clause misses is exactly L3.\n\nChasing `delegate_to` through role includes statically was rejected as brittle against `include_role`; a hand-pinned list is what #196 rejected.\n\n**Recorded boundary**: a future localhost-only playbook that delegates to the Proxmox host *without* importing L3 goes undetected. Acceptable — L3 is what establishes that SSH access, so such a playbook would not work anyway.\n\n**Consequence**: `bootstrap.yml` stops being a named exception. It is `hosts: localhost`, `connection: local`, imports no L3, and is non-live under either clause, so naming it was a no-op. The exception list is `controller-prerequisites.yml` alone.\n\n### 1.6 Lock contention keeps exit status 75\n\n`run.sh:26` exits **75** when it cannot take the lock. #193 standardised `0` success / `1` failed check or operation / `2` invalid usage, and no ticket reconciled the two.\n\n**The convention is `0` / `1` / `2` / `75`, where `75` means \"another holder has the lock\" and is returned by `./run.sh`, `./inspect.sh`, and `./recover.sh`.** #194 deliberately chose to stop rather than wait, and that choice only pays off if the caller can distinguish \"someone else is deploying\" from \"the deploy failed\". It also preserves existing behaviour, and `75` is `EX_TEMPFAIL`, which is what this is.\n\n`./inspect.sh vars` never returns `75` — it takes no lock.\n\n### 1.7 `./inspect.sh vars` derives the vault set from its own output\n\n#194's mask needs the decrypted vault key/value set for both detection rules, but #196 deleted the repository's only script-internal whole-vault decryption and #194's scope tripwire caps `vars` at one mask function plus one pass over an existing command's output.\n\n**The set is derived from the `ansible-inventory` output itself: every merged variable named `vault_*` is a vault key, and its value is a vault value for rule 2.** `group_vars/all/vault.yml` applies to every host, so all 40 keys are already present in the output — that is *why* it leaks 73 lines. No second decryption, no second input, tripwire intact.\n\nCost: rule 1 becomes \"named `vault_*`\" rather than \"a key in the vault\". So the prefix stops being a convention and becomes a stated contract in `inventory/group_vars/all/vault.yml.example`, and **test 8 asserts that every key in that file carries the prefix**. All 40 tracked keys conform today.\n\n**Recorded boundary** (in addition to #194's two): a vault key added without the `vault_` prefix is not masked by rule 1. Test 8 is what makes that a loud failure.\n\n---\n\n## 2. EVIDENCE POLICY
# Validation evidence reuse

Apply this policy whenever an implementation, readiness, Standards, Spec, or
closure context produces or adjudicates validation evidence. The frozen
Validation-surface manifest remains the complete population of direct evidence
the accepted candidate owes; this policy decides whether qualifying evidence
for a listed member must be executed again. It owns evidence identity,
sufficiency, invalidation, and reuse; it does not decide the workflow phase in
which evidence is executed. The selected workflow owns that timing, and this
policy applies when the owning phase is reached.

## Qualifying evidence

Candidate identity names the exact repository and all candidate-controlled
content under assessment. Include the base only when the validation depends on
the base or diff. Validation identity names the exact command, arguments,
working directory, and other check-defining inputs. Reusable-evidence identity
combines that Candidate identity and Validation identity with every relevant
environment, toolchain, external-input, and artifact identity whose change
could affect the result.

Reusable validation evidence supplies recoverable source provenance, execution
status, and inspectable raw output or a result artifact. A prior participant's
pass conclusion is not evidence. Every reviewer still makes a fresh Independent
judgment from the candidate, contract, and raw evidence without inheriting
prior conclusions, adjudications, or dispositions. Validity depends on identity
and provenance, not producer role.

Wave 1 uses a conservative exact-candidate rule. A committed HEAD qualifies
when the required worktree state is proven clean. Evidence from an uncommitted
state qualifies only when its content identity was deterministically captured
and proven identical to the reviewed candidate.

Evidence remains valid only for the candidate and inputs it exercised. Changes
to code, tests, fixtures, configuration, dependency locks, validation
definitions, relevant generated artifacts, external inputs, environment, or
toolchain state invalidate the evidence they can affect. When irrelevance is not
mechanically clear, obtain fresh evidence from the affected validation.

## Required execution

Assurance sufficiency alone determines whether another execution is required.
When qualifying evidence for the exact current Candidate identity and Validation
identity settles the concrete assurance question, another execution is not
required. When it does not, execute the narrowest check that settles it.

Independent execution is required when existing evidence cannot settle a
concrete assurance question involving timing, concurrency, nondeterminism,
environment- or host-sensitive behavior, uncertain identity or provenance,
incomplete, stale, contradictory, or otherwise suspect evidence,
or a finding that needs discriminating reproduction. A documented contract or
hard rule triggers re-execution only when it requires re-execution or its
assurance question cannot otherwise be resolved. Where the assurance question
itself requires an Independent context, implementation-context execution does
not satisfy it: at least one fresh Independent review context performs the
qualifying execution. Otherwise producer role does not determine validity.

Escalate in this order:

1. inspect the existing raw evidence;
2. use static or source inspection where sufficient;
3. run the cheapest adequate targeted discriminating check; and
4. use broader execution only when the narrower check cannot answer the
   assurance question.

Timing and concurrency require the smallest reproduction that establishes the
property, not an automatic full-suite rerun. "For confidence", "to be safe",
or independently repeating an already adequate green result do not justify
another execution. One qualifying Independent execution may answer several
named assurance questions and is never required once per reviewer or stage. A
workflow-stage transition is never itself a reason to execute again.

## Repetition guardrail

Only after sufficiency is established: do not repeat materially costly
deterministic validation already covered by qualifying evidence that settles the
current assurance question. Materially costly means repeating the validation
would meaningfully add workflow latency or consume a scarce resource. Judge that
qualitatively; never consult or build a duration threshold, timing history,
telemetry-based classification, cost database, or persistent resource metadata.

This is an efficiency directive, not an assurance invariant. Violating it wastes
resources; it does not by itself make the candidate or review unsound, and it is
never a reason to skip an execution sufficiency requires. Trivially cheap checks
stay at reviewer discretion. Do not move or pre-produce validation merely to
create reusable evidence.

## Validity across stages

A later workflow stage does not by itself make deterministic evidence stale.
Qualifying evidence may satisfy later stages and final closeout while its
complete Reusable-evidence identity remains unchanged. The final blind
confirmation still independently assesses the exact clean accepted candidate
and the sufficiency of its complete direct evidence; behavior- or
evidence-changing remediation invalidates that confirmation.

Failing, stale, contradictory, incomplete, identity-invalid, or otherwise
inadequate evidence remains blocking and never reaches the repetition
guardrail. Adjudicate what failed and the evidence's bearing on the contract
before another execution; a rerun-until-green chain without adjudication cannot
erase a failure. A documented hard-rule violation remains blocking, but does
not by itself require another execution.

## Safe evidence

Evidence records never persist credential or secret values and never override
privacy, redaction, retention, or access-control constraints. Record command
structure and declared environment inputs without their sensitive values; use
an opaque safe identifier or hash when a command, argument, artifact, input, or
environment detail is sensitive. A safe provenance locator may point to
access-controlled source evidence instead of copying it. Redact or avoid
retaining secret-bearing output under the governing constraints. Unsafe or
unrecoverable evidence is non-reusable: obtain safe qualifying evidence rather
than weakening those constraints.

## Reviewer record

Keep reuse and rerun reasoning in the ordinary reviewer report. For reused
evidence, record the Reusable-evidence identity, safe provenance locator, and
fresh Independent sufficiency judgment for the named criterion or assurance
question. For an execution claimed as necessary for Independent assurance, also
name the assurance question, why existing evidence and static inspection were
insufficient, and why the execution was the narrowest adequate check. A
discretionary cheap check owes no justification record.

Do not copy raw evidence into the Run telemetry sink or create another evidence
subsystem. Raw harness transcripts and access-controlled result artifacts
remain source evidence; the reviewer report carries safe provenance and
reasoning only.

# Homelab Infrastructure Lifecycle

This context describes how the repository plans and applies changes to the managed homelab infrastructure.

## Language

**Image update track**:
An operator-selected version or release line used to discover eligible updates for one effective Compose image. An image-tracked stack can declare a shared default and service-specific exceptions, but every image-bearing service must have an intentional effective image update track.
_Avoid_: Channel, version inferred from the current tag

**Repository input snapshot**:
A read-only, schema-versioned record that authorizes the clone's current `HEAD` only when it equals GitHub's current default-branch commit, then fingerprints the checked-in policy, supported Compose inputs, and checked-in-policy-assisted runbook relevant to each operator-selected repo-managed stack. Unrelated worktree changes remain usable; changed relevant inputs make only their stack incomplete.
_Avoid_: Image update plan, deployed-state snapshot, validation result

**Repo-managed stack identity**:
The pair of inventory hostname and Compose project name that uniquely identifies one repo-managed stack across scans and image update proposals.
_Avoid_: Proposal title, image name

**Stack update policy**:
The operator-authored rules for detecting and preparing an image update proposal for one repo-managed stack. It identifies the upstream authority and update procedure for the stack, with optional per-image update-track and compatibility rules.
_Avoid_: Global image policy, deployment policy

**Stack tracking mode**:
The stack update policy choice between following independently managed image references and following an official upstream Compose baseline.
_Avoid_: Update ownership, portability owner

**Image-tracked stack**:
A repo-managed stack whose Compose definition is owned independently in this repository and whose update policy follows the container images referenced by that definition.
_Avoid_: Vendor-tracked stack, unmanaged stack

**Vendor-tracked stack**:
A repo-managed stack whose base Compose file deliberately follows a suitable official upstream Compose file, while homelab-specific behavior is isolated in an override layer. Its image update proposals compare the upstream baseline and identify any override adaptations required.
_Avoid_: Vendored stack, independently maintained stack

**Image update scan request**:
A Renovate-independent selection of validated stack and service identities, current image references, image update tracks, and candidate constraints. The Renovate adapter translates it into a scan projection and tool-specific configuration.
_Avoid_: Renovate configuration, stack update policy

**Image update scan projection**:
A disposable, stack-identity-preserving Compose representation generated from validated effective Compose models and stack update policies for a Renovate adapter run. It is lookup input only and never repository desired state.
_Avoid_: Generated stack, proposed Compose file, deployment manifest

**Renovate adapter**:
The pinned, read-only boundary that translates stack update policy into a local Renovate dry run and normalizes Renovate's results. Raw Renovate output and its version-specific shape do not cross this boundary.
_Avoid_: Renovate integration, registry client

**Image update candidate observation**:
A normalized account of one Compose service's current image and Renovate-selected candidate, including comparable digests, update classification, proposed exact reference, available release context, and lookup limitations. It supplies facts to proposal readiness evaluation but does not assign an outcome or change repository files.
_Avoid_: Renovate record, proposed patch, proposal readiness outcome

**Core candidate evidence**:
The minimum proof required before an image update candidate may produce or refresh a proposal: a valid effective policy and update track, comparable current and candidate digests, proof of a differing eligible candidate, and, for vendor-tracked stacks, an upstream Compose baseline resolved at a commit.
_Avoid_: Release enrichment, confidence context

**Targeted LXC set**:
The managed LXCs selected for a lifecycle run. Safety checks and the pre-action planning barrier apply to this set, not automatically to every LXC in inventory.
_Avoid_: Fleet, all LXCs

**Fleet preflight**:
The planning phase that validates cross-LXC invariants and shared infrastructure access, then provides a common observation of Proxmox state. It does not decide the lifecycle transition for an individual LXC.
_Avoid_: Per-LXC validation, lifecycle planning

**LXC identity reservation**:
An inventory claim on the VMID and hostname of a managed LXC, whether or not that LXC is targeted or currently exists. A targeted lifecycle run cannot use an identity reserved by another managed LXC.
_Avoid_: Runtime identity, active-container identity

**LXC lifecycle plan**:
A validated, non-executing description of the semantic transitions required to bring one targeted LXC from its observed state to its desired state, including destructive intent and reasons without exposing internal task names. It belongs only to the lifecycle run that produced it and is not reusable by a later run.
_Avoid_: Validation snapshot, action lists

**LXC lifecycle result**:
The semantic record of an LXC lifecycle plan and its observable execution outcome, with compact before-and-after observations. Every targeted LXC receives a result, including targets blocked from execution by another target's planning failure; results exclude internal task names, intermediate facts, and duplicated compiled contract data.
_Avoid_: Internal snapshot, action report

**LXC contract compilation**:
The single interpretation of layered inventory into the authoritative desired infrastructure state for one LXC. Infrastructure validation, provisioning, host configuration, and guest bootstrap consume the resulting compiled LXC contract rather than interpreting the inventory layers again.
_Avoid_: Flattening, spec merge

**Manual SSH recovery**:
An operator-initiated access restoration operation for an existing LXC. It remains usable when unrelated desired infrastructure state is invalid.
_Avoid_: Normal lifecycle configuration, full convergence

**Managed host configuration**:
The portion of an LXC's Proxmox-host configuration whose complete desired state is expressed by the compiled LXC contract. Manual changes within a managed category are not durable; configuration outside managed categories remains untouched.
_Avoid_: Additive configuration, minimum configuration

**Guest-command readiness**:
The proof that an LXC accepts a minimal command executed inside it through the Proxmox host. It is bounded by a deadline and is the only readiness managed host configuration establishes after a restart. It does not imply SSH access, boot completion, or application health; those remain owned by the modules that require them, and SSH access stays owned by the guest-configuration connection wait.
_Avoid_: Container running, boot complete, SSH ready

**LXC observation**:
A point-in-time representation of an LXC's current infrastructure and runtime state, used to compare reality with its compiled desired state.
_Avoid_: Validation snapshot, independently queried state

**Lifecycle planning barrier**:
The safety guarantee that no lifecycle actions begin until every targeted LXC has a valid LXC lifecycle plan. A planning failure for any target prevents actions for the entire targeted LXC set.
_Avoid_: Strict-validation mode, partial-skip execution

**Lifecycle policy**:
Persistent operator-authored rules that determine whether observed drift may produce destructive lifecycle transitions. A valid plan executes without a second per-run confirmation when its destructive transition is authorized by policy.
_Avoid_: Interactive approval, per-run confirmation

**Lifecycle intent**:
The exact set of infrastructure and configuration transitions permitted for a lifecycle run. If the requested outcome requires a transition outside that set, lifecycle planning fails rather than silently skipping it.
_Avoid_: Best-effort mode, lifecycle hint

**Configure-only lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles configuration without creating or starting an LXC. Every targeted LXC must already be running or the run fails at the lifecycle planning barrier.
_Avoid_: Best-effort configuration, start-and-configure

**Provision-only lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles LXC existence and managed host configuration without guest configuration. It starts an LXC when creating or rebuilding it but preserves the stopped state of an existing LXC.
_Avoid_: Ensure-running lifecycle, guest configuration

**Full lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles both LXC infrastructure and guest configuration. It may start an existing stopped LXC because guest configuration requires the LXC to be running.
_Avoid_: Provision-only lifecycle, configure-only lifecycle

**Workstation setup marker**:
The record written by a completed workstation setup run, holding the identity of the inputs that run applied. It is the authority consulted before any work begins, so an input the marker does not record is an input no later run can detect a change to.
_Avoid_: Completion flag, sentinel file, done marker

**Workstation tool readiness**:
The proof that the workstation's required commands are present, runnable, and resolved from their managed locations. It says nothing about which declared configuration produced those commands.
_Avoid_: Environment healthy, validated environment, workstation configuration freshness

**Workstation configuration freshness**:
Whether the workstation's active Home Manager generation was built from the currently checked-out dotfiles source. It is evaluated against the local checkout only, never against the remote, and it is independent of workstation tool readiness — working tools prove nothing about it.
_Avoid_: Drift, environment health, in sync with origin

FILE docs/adr/0001-preserve-linear-lxc-execution.md
# Preserve linear LXC execution until dependencies are explicit

LXC lifecycle execution remains linear even after planning is separated from execution, and the first execution failure aborts remaining work for the targeted LXC set without attempting rollback. Independent per-LXC execution is deferred until stack and LXC dependencies—including required ordering, failure propagation, readiness, and reverse removal ordering—are represented explicitly and validated as an acyclic graph; Ansible's `free` strategy alone cannot provide those guarantees. A future dependency-aware scheduler may replace global fail-fast behavior with branch-scoped failure propagation, allowing genuinely independent branches to continue.

FILE docs/adr/0002-keep-manual-ssh-recovery-minimal.md
# Keep manual SSH recovery independent of full contract compilation

Manual SSH recovery validates only the identity and public key needed to restore access to an existing LXC, then uses the same guest-bootstrap implementation as normal lifecycle execution. It must not require the full compiled LXC contract because unrelated invalid infrastructure state could otherwise block the recovery operation.

FILE docs/adr/0003-make-managed-host-configuration-authoritative.md
# Make managed host configuration authoritative

Each host-configuration category represented in the compiled LXC contract is a complete desired set, not an additive minimum. Reconciliation removes undeclared settings within managed categories, overwrites manual changes there, preserves unrelated configuration, and compares normalized semantic state so Proxmox line reordering does not cause false changes or restarts.

FILE docs/adr/0004-require-valid-plans-for-all-targeted-lxcs.md
# Require valid plans for every targeted LXC

Full lifecycle execution crosses the lifecycle planning barrier only when every targeted LXC has a valid plan; any compilation, identity, required-observation, or unsatisfied intent precondition blocks actions for the entire targeted set. Lifecycle intent is a strict set of permitted transitions: if the requested outcome requires a transition outside that set, planning fails instead of silently skipping it. Configure-only lifecycle therefore requires every target to be running rather than silently skipping absent or stopped LXCs. When release-based rebuild policy is enabled, the guest release is a required observation and an unprobeable stopped target blocks planning; when that policy is disabled, release observation is not required. Every target still receives a semantic result when the barrier blocks execution, distinguishing the planning failure from otherwise valid plans that were not executed. This replaces partial-skip execution for planning failures. Standalone validation aggregates all detected problems before exiting nonzero when any planning failure exists, and command limits keep unrelated inventory hosts outside the barrier.

FILE docs/adr/0005-use-persistent-policy-for-destructive-lifecycle-plans.md
# Use persistent policy for destructive lifecycle plans

A destructive LXC lifecycle plan executes in the same full lifecycle run when persistent inventory policy explicitly authorizes its transition; no interactive or per-run confirmation is added. Destructive behavior remains disabled by default, and the lifecycle planning barrier must still produce valid plans for every targeted LXC before any authorized action begins.

FILE docs/adr/0006-separate-fleet-preflight-from-lxc-lifecycle-planning.md
# Separate fleet preflight from LXC lifecycle planning

Fleet preflight consumes compiled identities, validates cross-LXC invariants and shared infrastructure access, and obtains one common Proxmox observation. Identity reservations are checked across all managed inventory hosts, while unrelated full-contract validity is required only for the targeted LXC set. Fleet preflight does not otherwise interpret raw desired-state inventory or decide per-LXC transitions; comparison, release classification, and semantic plan construction belong to the LXC lifecycle module.

FILE docs/adr/0007-keep-lxc-lifecycle-policy-in-ansible.md
# Keep LXC lifecycle policy in Ansible

LXC contract compilation, semantic lifecycle planning, and execution remain Ansible-native so the repository retains one architectural center for infrastructure convergence. Lifecycle scenarios, inputs, semantic assertions, and decisions therefore stay in Ansible. Python may select, schedule, launch, report, and test the orchestration of the standalone lifecycle regression launchers, but it may not reimplement lifecycle policy or use Python assertions as a substitute for Ansible-native semantic coverage.

The semantic lifecycle plan is the stable interface and test surface; moving core policy into Python requires demonstrated pressure such as repeated type-related bugs, duplicated decisions, or an unmanageable Ansible scenario matrix rather than anticipated future growth.

   - Failing observation: the decision is missing, does not place enforcement at `validate.sh`, omits the rejected per-fixture and offline alternatives, or omits the no-managed-host/no-vault-secret/no-machine-specific-credential and public-network boundaries.
   - Validation surface: the complete exact ADR file above.

9. **`./validate.sh` passes.**
   - Production path: the complete committed candidate.
   - Direct seam: execute the exact real no-argument `./validate.sh` from the repository root.
   - Failing observation: nonzero exit status.
   - Validation surface: one complete no-argument `./validate.sh` run for the exact final candidate; the empty-home execution for criterion 4 may supply the same qualifying raw execution when identities match.

## Owed validation and phase ownership

- **Implementation:** red-green focused checks for `tests/regression/test_validate_command.py`, `tests/unit/test_lxc_lifecycle_regression_runner.py`, and the helper's focused test module; narrow YAML/static inspection for the fixture inventory; keep raw output as candidate-bound evidence.
- **Primary checkpoint / initial-gate path:** rerun only invalidated focused checks after readiness corrections and populate direct evidence for every frozen member not already settled by qualifying exact-candidate evidence.
- **Gate:** fresh Standards, Spec, and cumulative closure judgments consume the complete frozen surface and qualifying raw evidence; they do not execute a full regression merely because the gate began.
- **Remediation:** only focused checks and frozen members invalidated by an accepted corrective batch; no full regression.
- **Closeout:** run the complete no-argument `./validate.sh` under a fresh empty `HOME` with no machine-local vault passphrase, satisfying criteria 4 and 9 when green; run `git diff --check`. Reuse that exact qualifying full-run evidence rather than executing `./validate.sh` twice.

The repository-required full handoff command is owned by Closeout. It is not an implementation-completion prerequisite and must not be pre-produced for reuse.

EVIDENCE POLICY
# Validation evidence reuse

Apply this policy whenever an implementation, readiness, Standards, Spec, or
closure context produces or adjudicates validation evidence. The frozen
Validation-surface manifest remains the complete population of direct evidence
the accepted candidate owes; this policy decides whether qualifying evidence
for a listed member must be executed again. It owns evidence identity,
sufficiency, invalidation, and reuse; it does not decide the workflow phase in
which evidence is executed. The selected workflow owns that timing, and this
policy applies when the owning phase is reached.

## Qualifying evidence

Candidate identity names the exact repository and all candidate-controlled
content under assessment. Include the base only when the validation depends on
the base or diff. Validation identity names the exact command, arguments,
working directory, and other check-defining inputs. Reusable-evidence identity
combines that Candidate identity and Validation identity with every relevant
environment, toolchain, external-input, and artifact identity whose change
could affect the result.

Reusable validation evidence supplies recoverable source provenance, execution
status, and inspectable raw output or a result artifact. A prior participant's
pass conclusion is not evidence. Every reviewer still makes a fresh Independent
judgment from the candidate, contract, and raw evidence without inheriting
prior conclusions, adjudications, or dispositions. Validity depends on identity
and provenance, not producer role.

Wave 1 uses a conservative exact-candidate rule. A committed HEAD qualifies
when the required worktree state is proven clean. Evidence from an uncommitted
state qualifies only when its content identity was deterministically captured
and proven identical to the reviewed candidate.

Evidence remains valid only for the candidate and inputs it exercised. Changes
to code, tests, fixtures, configuration, dependency locks, validation
definitions, relevant generated artifacts, external inputs, environment, or
toolchain state invalidate the evidence they can affect. When irrelevance is not
mechanically clear, obtain fresh evidence from the affected validation.

## Required execution

Assurance sufficiency alone determines whether another execution is required.
When qualifying evidence for the exact current Candidate identity and Validation
identity settles the concrete assurance question, another execution is not
required. When it does not, execute the narrowest check that settles it.

Independent execution is required when existing evidence cannot settle a
concrete assurance question involving timing, concurrency, nondeterminism,
environment- or host-sensitive behavior, uncertain identity or provenance,
incomplete, stale, contradictory, or otherwise suspect evidence,
or a finding that needs discriminating reproduction. A documented contract or
hard rule triggers re-execution only when it requires re-execution or its
assurance question cannot otherwise be resolved. Where the assurance question
itself requires an Independent context, implementation-context execution does
not satisfy it: at least one fresh Independent review context performs the
qualifying execution. Otherwise producer role does not determine validity.

Escalate in this order:

1. inspect the existing raw evidence;
2. use static or source inspection where sufficient;
3. run the cheapest adequate targeted discriminating check; and
4. use broader execution only when the narrower check cannot answer the
   assurance question.

Timing and concurrency require the smallest reproduction that establishes the
property, not an automatic full-suite rerun. "For confidence", "to be safe",
or independently repeating an already adequate green result do not justify
another execution. One qualifying Independent execution may answer several
named assurance questions and is never required once per reviewer or stage. A
workflow-stage transition is never itself a reason to execute again.

## Repetition guardrail

Only after sufficiency is established: do not repeat materially costly
deterministic validation already covered by qualifying evidence that settles the
current assurance question. Materially costly means repeating the validation
would meaningfully add workflow latency or consume a scarce resource. Judge that
qualitatively; never consult or build a duration threshold, timing history,
telemetry-based classification, cost database, or persistent resource metadata.

This is an efficiency directive, not an assurance invariant. Violating it wastes
resources; it does not by itself make the candidate or review unsound, and it is
never a reason to skip an execution sufficiency requires. Trivially cheap checks
stay at reviewer discretion. Do not move or pre-produce validation merely to
create reusable evidence.

## Validity across stages

A later workflow stage does not by itself make deterministic evidence stale.
Qualifying evidence may satisfy later stages and final closeout while its
complete Reusable-evidence identity remains unchanged. The final blind
confirmation still independently assesses the exact clean accepted candidate
and the sufficiency of its complete direct evidence; behavior- or
evidence-changing remediation invalidates that confirmation.

Failing, stale, contradictory, incomplete, identity-invalid, or otherwise
inadequate evidence remains blocking and never reaches the repetition
guardrail. Adjudicate what failed and the evidence's bearing on the contract
before another execution; a rerun-until-green chain without adjudication cannot
erase a failure. A documented hard-rule violation remains blocking, but does
not by itself require another execution.

## Safe evidence

Evidence records never persist credential or secret values and never override
privacy, redaction, retention, or access-control constraints. Record command
structure and declared environment inputs without their sensitive values; use
an opaque safe identifier or hash when a command, argument, artifact, input, or
environment detail is sensitive. A safe provenance locator may point to
access-controlled source evidence instead of copying it. Redact or avoid
retaining secret-bearing output under the governing constraints. Unsafe or
unrecoverable evidence is non-reusable: obtain safe qualifying evidence rather
than weakening those constraints.

## Reviewer record

Keep reuse and rerun reasoning in the ordinary reviewer report. For reused
evidence, record the Reusable-evidence identity, safe provenance locator, and
fresh Independent sufficiency judgment for the named criterion or assurance
question. For an execution claimed as necessary for Independent assurance, also
name the assurance question, why existing evidence and static inspection were
insufficient, and why the execution was the narrowest adequate check. A
discretionary cheap check owes no justification record.

Do not copy raw evidence into the Run telemetry sink or create another evidence
subsystem. Raw harness transcripts and access-controlled result artifacts
remain source evidence; the reviewer report carries safe provenance and
reasoning only.

# Homelab Infrastructure Lifecycle

This context describes how the repository plans and applies changes to the managed homelab infrastructure.

## Language

**Image update track**:
An operator-selected version or release line used to discover eligible updates for one effective Compose image. An image-tracked stack can declare a shared default and service-specific exceptions, but every image-bearing service must have an intentional effective image update track.
_Avoid_: Channel, version inferred from the current tag

**Repository input snapshot**:
A read-only, schema-versioned record that authorizes the clone's current `HEAD` only when it equals GitHub's current default-branch commit, then fingerprints the checked-in policy, supported Compose inputs, and checked-in-policy-assisted runbook relevant to each operator-selected repo-managed stack. Unrelated worktree changes remain usable; changed relevant inputs make only their stack incomplete.
_Avoid_: Image update plan, deployed-state snapshot, validation result

**Repo-managed stack identity**:
The pair of inventory hostname and Compose project name that uniquely identifies one repo-managed stack across scans and image update proposals.
_Avoid_: Proposal title, image name

**Stack update policy**:
The operator-authored rules for detecting and preparing an image update proposal for one repo-managed stack. It identifies the upstream authority and update procedure for the stack, with optional per-image update-track and compatibility rules.
_Avoid_: Global image policy, deployment policy

**Stack tracking mode**:
The stack update policy choice between following independently managed image references and following an official upstream Compose baseline.
_Avoid_: Update ownership, portability owner

**Image-tracked stack**:
A repo-managed stack whose Compose definition is owned independently in this repository and whose update policy follows the container images referenced by that definition.
_Avoid_: Vendor-tracked stack, unmanaged stack

**Vendor-tracked stack**:
A repo-managed stack whose base Compose file deliberately follows a suitable official upstream Compose file, while homelab-specific behavior is isolated in an override layer. Its image update proposals compare the upstream baseline and identify any override adaptations required.
_Avoid_: Vendored stack, independently maintained stack

**Image update scan request**:
A Renovate-independent selection of validated stack and service identities, current image references, image update tracks, and candidate constraints. The Renovate adapter translates it into a scan projection and tool-specific configuration.
_Avoid_: Renovate configuration, stack update policy

**Image update scan projection**:
A disposable, stack-identity-preserving Compose representation generated from validated effective Compose models and stack update policies for a Renovate adapter run. It is lookup input only and never repository desired state.
_Avoid_: Generated stack, proposed Compose file, deployment manifest

**Renovate adapter**:
The pinned, read-only boundary that translates stack update policy into a local Renovate dry run and normalizes Renovate's results. Raw Renovate output and its version-specific shape do not cross this boundary.
_Avoid_: Renovate integration, registry client

**Image update candidate observation**:
A normalized account of one Compose service's current image and Renovate-selected candidate, including comparable digests, update classification, proposed exact reference, available release context, and lookup limitations. It supplies facts to proposal readiness evaluation but does not assign an outcome or change repository files.
_Avoid_: Renovate record, proposed patch, proposal readiness outcome

**Core candidate evidence**:
The minimum proof required before an image update candidate may produce or refresh a proposal: a valid effective policy and update track, comparable current and candidate digests, proof of a differing eligible candidate, and, for vendor-tracked stacks, an upstream Compose baseline resolved at a commit.
_Avoid_: Release enrichment, confidence context

**Targeted LXC set**:
The managed LXCs selected for a lifecycle run. Safety checks and the pre-action planning barrier apply to this set, not automatically to every LXC in inventory.
_Avoid_: Fleet, all LXCs

**Fleet preflight**:
The planning phase that validates cross-LXC invariants and shared infrastructure access, then provides a common observation of Proxmox state. It does not decide the lifecycle transition for an individual LXC.
_Avoid_: Per-LXC validation, lifecycle planning

**LXC identity reservation**:
An inventory claim on the VMID and hostname of a managed LXC, whether or not that LXC is targeted or currently exists. A targeted lifecycle run cannot use an identity reserved by another managed LXC.
_Avoid_: Runtime identity, active-container identity

**LXC lifecycle plan**:
A validated, non-executing description of the semantic transitions required to bring one targeted LXC from its observed state to its desired state, including destructive intent and reasons without exposing internal task names. It belongs only to the lifecycle run that produced it and is not reusable by a later run.
_Avoid_: Validation snapshot, action lists

**LXC lifecycle result**:
The semantic record of an LXC lifecycle plan and its observable execution outcome, with compact before-and-after observations. Every targeted LXC receives a result, including targets blocked from execution by another target's planning failure; results exclude internal task names, intermediate facts, and duplicated compiled contract data.
_Avoid_: Internal snapshot, action report

**LXC contract compilation**:
The single interpretation of layered inventory into the authoritative desired infrastructure state for one LXC. Infrastructure validation, provisioning, host configuration, and guest bootstrap consume the resulting compiled LXC contract rather than interpreting the inventory layers again.
_Avoid_: Flattening, spec merge

**Manual SSH recovery**:
An operator-initiated access restoration operation for an existing LXC. It remains usable when unrelated desired infrastructure state is invalid.
_Avoid_: Normal lifecycle configuration, full convergence

**Managed host configuration**:
The portion of an LXC's Proxmox-host configuration whose complete desired state is expressed by the compiled LXC contract. Manual changes within a managed category are not durable; configuration outside managed categories remains untouched.
_Avoid_: Additive configuration, minimum configuration

**Guest-command readiness**:
The proof that an LXC accepts a minimal command executed inside it through the Proxmox host. It is bounded by a deadline and is the only readiness managed host configuration establishes after a restart. It does not imply SSH access, boot completion, or application health; those remain owned by the modules that require them, and SSH access stays owned by the guest-configuration connection wait.
_Avoid_: Container running, boot complete, SSH ready

**LXC observation**:
A point-in-time representation of an LXC's current infrastructure and runtime state, used to compare reality with its compiled desired state.
_Avoid_: Validation snapshot, independently queried state

**Lifecycle planning barrier**:
The safety guarantee that no lifecycle actions begin until every targeted LXC has a valid LXC lifecycle plan. A planning failure for any target prevents actions for the entire targeted LXC set.
_Avoid_: Strict-validation mode, partial-skip execution

**Lifecycle policy**:
Persistent operator-authored rules that determine whether observed drift may produce destructive lifecycle transitions. A valid plan executes without a second per-run confirmation when its destructive transition is authorized by policy.
_Avoid_: Interactive approval, per-run confirmation

**Lifecycle intent**:
The exact set of infrastructure and configuration transitions permitted for a lifecycle run. If the requested outcome requires a transition outside that set, lifecycle planning fails rather than silently skipping it.
_Avoid_: Best-effort mode, lifecycle hint

**Configure-only lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles configuration without creating or starting an LXC. Every targeted LXC must already be running or the run fails at the lifecycle planning barrier.
_Avoid_: Best-effort configuration, start-and-configure

**Provision-only lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles LXC existence and managed host configuration without guest configuration. It starts an LXC when creating or rebuilding it but preserves the stopped state of an existing LXC.
_Avoid_: Ensure-running lifecycle, guest configuration

**Full lifecycle**:
A lifecycle run that reconciles both LXC infrastructure and guest configuration. It may start an existing stopped LXC because guest configuration requires the LXC to be running.
_Avoid_: Provision-only lifecycle, configure-only lifecycle

**Workstation setup marker**:
The record written by a completed workstation setup run, holding the identity of the inputs that run applied. It is the authority consulted before any work begins, so an input the marker does not record is an input no later run can detect a change to.
_Avoid_: Completion flag, sentinel file, done marker

**Workstation tool readiness**:
The proof that the workstation's required commands are present, runnable, and resolved from their managed locations. It says nothing about which declared configuration produced those commands.
_Avoid_: Environment healthy, validated environment, workstation configuration freshness

**Workstation configuration freshness**:
Whether the workstation's active Home Manager generation was built from the currently checked-out dotfiles source. It is evaluated against the local checkout only, never against the remote, and it is independent of workstation tool readiness — working tools prove nothing about it.
_Avoid_: Drift, environment health, in sync with origin

FILE docs/adr/0001-preserve-linear-lxc-execution.md
# Preserve linear LXC execution until dependencies are explicit

LXC lifecycle execution remains linear even after planning is separated from execution, and the first execution failure aborts remaining work for the targeted LXC set without attempting rollback. Independent per-LXC execution is deferred until stack and LXC dependencies—including required ordering, failure propagation, readiness, and reverse removal ordering—are represented explicitly and validated as an acyclic graph; Ansible's `free` strategy alone cannot provide those guarantees. A future dependency-aware scheduler may replace global fail-fast behavior with branch-scoped failure propagation, allowing genuinely independent branches to continue.

FILE docs/adr/0002-keep-manual-ssh-recovery-minimal.md
# Keep manual SSH recovery independent of full contract compilation

Manual SSH recovery validates only the identity and public key needed to restore access to an existing LXC, then uses the same guest-bootstrap implementation as normal lifecycle execution. It must not require the full compiled LXC contract because unrelated invalid infrastructure state could otherwise block the recovery operation.

FILE docs/adr/0003-make-managed-host-configuration-authoritative.md
# Make managed host configuration authoritative

Each host-configuration category represented in the compiled LXC contract is a complete desired set, not an additive minimum. Reconciliation removes undeclared settings within managed categories, overwrites manual changes there, preserves unrelated configuration, and compares normalized semantic state so Proxmox line reordering does not cause false changes or restarts.

FILE docs/adr/0004-require-valid-plans-for-all-targeted-lxcs.md
# Require valid plans for every targeted LXC

Full lifecycle execution crosses the lifecycle planning barrier only when every targeted LXC has a valid plan; any compilation, identity, required-observation, or unsatisfied intent precondition blocks actions for the entire targeted set. Lifecycle intent is a strict set of permitted transitions: if the requested outcome requires a transition outside that set, planning fails instead of silently skipping it. Configure-only lifecycle therefore requires every target to be running rather than silently skipping absent or stopped LXCs. When release-based rebuild policy is enabled, the guest release is a required observation and an unprobeable stopped target blocks planning; when that policy is disabled, release observation is not required. Every target still receives a semantic result when the barrier blocks execution, distinguishing the planning failure from otherwise valid plans that were not executed. This replaces partial-skip execution for planning failures. Standalone validation aggregates all detected problems before exiting nonzero when any planning failure exists, and command limits keep unrelated inventory hosts outside the barrier.

FILE docs/adr/0005-use-persistent-policy-for-destructive-lifecycle-plans.md
# Use persistent policy for destructive lifecycle plans

A destructive LXC lifecycle plan executes in the same full lifecycle run when persistent inventory policy explicitly authorizes its transition; no interactive or per-run confirmation is added. Destructive behavior remains disabled by default, and the lifecycle planning barrier must still produce valid plans for every targeted LXC before any authorized action begins.

FILE docs/adr/0006-separate-fleet-preflight-from-lxc-lifecycle-planning.md
# Separate fleet preflight from LXC lifecycle planning

Fleet preflight consumes compiled identities, validates cross-LXC invariants and shared infrastructure access, and obtains one common Proxmox observation. Identity reservations are checked across all managed inventory hosts, while unrelated full-contract validity is required only for the targeted LXC set. Fleet preflight does not otherwise interpret raw desired-state inventory or decide per-LXC transitions; comparison, release classification, and semantic plan construction belong to the LXC lifecycle module.

FILE docs/adr/0007-keep-lxc-lifecycle-policy-in-ansible.md
# Keep LXC lifecycle policy in Ansible

LXC contract compilation, semantic lifecycle planning, and execution remain Ansible-native so the repository retains one architectural center for infrastructure convergence. Lifecycle scenarios, inputs, semantic assertions, and decisions therefore stay in Ansible. Python may select, schedule, launch, report, and test the orchestration of the standalone lifecycle regression launchers, but it may not reimplement lifecycle policy or use Python assertions as a substitute for Ansible-native semantic coverage.

The semantic lifecycle plan is the stable interface and test surface; moving core policy into Python requires demonstrated pressure such as repeated type-related bugs, duplicated decisions, or an unmanageable Ansible scenario matrix rather than anticipated future growth.

EVIDENCE POLICY
# Validation evidence reuse

Apply this policy whenever an implementation, readiness, Standards, Spec, or
closure context produces or adjudicates validation evidence. The frozen
Validation-surface manifest remains the complete population of direct evidence
the accepted candidate owes; this policy decides whether qualifying evidence
for a listed member must be executed again. It owns evidence identity,
sufficiency, invalidation, and reuse; it does not decide the workflow phase in
which evidence is executed. The selected workflow owns that timing, and this
policy applies when the owning phase is reached.

## Qualifying evidence

Candidate identity names the exact repository and all candidate-controlled
content under assessment. Include the base only when the validation depends on
the base or diff. Validation identity names the exact command, arguments,
working directory, and other check-defining inputs. Reusable-evidence identity
combines that Candidate identity and Validation identity with every relevant
environment, toolchain, external-input, and artifact identity whose change
could affect the result.

Reusable validation evidence supplies recoverable source provenance, execution
status, and inspectable raw output or a result artifact. A prior participant's
pass conclusion is not evidence. Every reviewer still makes a fresh Independent
judgment from the candidate, contract, and raw evidence without inheriting
prior conclusions, adjudications, or dispositions. Validity depends on identity
and provenance, not producer role.

Wave 1 uses a conservative exact-candidate rule. A committed HEAD qualifies
when the required worktree state is proven clean. Evidence from an uncommitted
state qualifies only when its content identity was deterministically captured
and proven identical to the reviewed candidate.

Evidence remains valid only for the candidate and inputs it exercised. Changes
to code, tests, fixtures, configuration, dependency locks, validation
definitions, relevant generated artifacts, external inputs, environment, or
toolchain state invalidate the evidence they can affect. When irrelevance is not
mechanically clear, obtain fresh evidence from the affected validation.

## Required execution

Assurance sufficiency alone determines whether another execution is required.
When qualifying evidence for the exact current Candidate identity and Validation
identity settles the concrete assurance question, another execution is not
required. When it does not, execute the narrowest check that settles it.

Independent execution is required when existing evidence cannot settle a
concrete assurance question involving timing, concurrency, nondeterminism,
environment- or host-sensitive behavior, uncertain identity or provenance,
incomplete, stale, contradictory, or otherwise suspect evidence,
or a finding that needs discriminating reproduction. A documented contract or
hard rule triggers re-execution only when it requires re-execution or its
assurance question cannot otherwise be resolved. Where the assurance question
itself requires an Independent context, implementation-context execution does
not satisfy it: at least one fresh Independent review context performs the
qualifying execution. Otherwise producer role does not determine validity.

Escalate in this order:

1. inspect the existing raw evidence;
2. use static or source inspection where sufficient;
3. run the cheapest adequate targeted discriminating check; and
4. use broader execution only when the narrower check cannot answer the
   assurance question.

Timing and concurrency require the smallest reproduction that establishes the
property, not an automatic full-suite rerun. "For confidence", "to be safe",
or independently repeating an already adequate green result do not justify
another execution. One qualifying Independent execution may answer several
named assurance questions and is never required once per reviewer or stage. A
workflow-stage transition is never itself a reason to execute again.

## Repetition guardrail

Only after sufficiency is established: do not repeat materially costly
deterministic validation already covered by qualifying evidence that settles the
current assurance question. Materially costly means repeating the validation
would meaningfully add workflow latency or consume a scarce resource. Judge that
qualitatively; never consult or build a duration threshold, timing history,
telemetry-based classification, cost database, or persistent resource metadata.

This is an efficiency directive, not an assurance invariant. Violating it wastes
resources; it does not by itself make the candidate or review unsound, and it is
never a reason to skip an execution sufficiency requires. Trivially cheap checks
stay at reviewer discretion. Do not move or pre-produce validation merely to
create reusable evidence.

## Validity across stages

A later workflow stage does not by itself make deterministic evidence stale.
Qualifying evidence may satisfy later stages and final closeout while its
complete Reusable-evidence identity remains unchanged. The final blind
confirmation still independently assesses the exact clean accepted candidate
and the sufficiency of its complete direct evidence; behavior- or
evidence-changing remediation invalidates that confirmation.

Failing, stale, contradictory, incomplete, identity-invalid, or otherwise
inadequate evidence remains blocking and never reaches the repetition
guardrail. Adjudicate what failed and the evidence's bearing on the contract
before another execution; a rerun-until-green chain without adjudication cannot
erase a failure. A documented hard-rule violation remains blocking, but does
not by itself require another execution.

## Safe evidence

Evidence records never persist credential or secret values and never override
privacy, redaction, retention, or access-control constraints. Record command
structure and declared environment inputs without their sensitive values; use
an opaque safe identifier or hash when a command, argument, artifact, input, or
environment detail is sensitive. A safe provenance locator may point to
access-controlled source evidence instead of copying it. Redact or avoid
retaining secret-bearing output under the governing constraints. Unsafe or
unrecoverable evidence is non-reusable: obtain safe qualifying evidence rather
than weakening those constraints.

## Reviewer record

Keep reuse and rerun reasoning in the ordinary reviewer report. For reused
evidence, record the Reusable-evidence identity, safe provenance locator, and
fresh Independent sufficiency judgment for the named criterion or assurance
question. For an execution claimed as necessary for Independent assurance, also
name the assurance question, why existing evidence and static inspection were
insufficient, and why the execution was the narrowest adequate check. A
discretionary cheap check owes no justification record.

Do not copy raw evidence into the Run telemetry sink or create another evidence
subsystem. Raw harness transcripts and access-controlled result artifacts
remain source evidence; the reviewer report carries safe provenance and
reasoning only.
